en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammapaccanīya (2), Dukadukapaṭṭhānapāḷi (6) 12.7.
Sahetukadukādi, Hetuduka (The Section on the Root-Dyads, beginning with the Dyad on Being With a Root-Cause)
Dependent on a state that is neither with root-cause nor a root-cause, a state that is neither with root-cause nor a root-cause arises by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is neither with root-cause nor a root-cause, a state that is without root-cause but not a root-cause arises by way of root-condition.

Dependent on a state that is neither with root-cause nor a root-cause, states that are both neither with root-cause nor a root-cause and without root-cause but not a root-cause arise [by way of root-condition].
They arise by way of root-condition (hetu-paccaya). Dependent on a state that is neither-rooted nor a root, there arises a state that is neither-rooted nor a root by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is neither-rooted nor a root, there arises a state that is not-with-root but is not a root by way of root-condition.

Dependent on a state that is neither-with-root-cause nor root-cause, there arise states that are both not-with-root-cause and not-root-cause, and states that are neither-with-root-cause and not-root-cause, by way of root-condition.

Dependent on a state that is not-with-root-cause and not-root-cause, and a state that is neither-with-root-cause and not-root-cause, there arises a state that is not-with-root-cause and not-root-cause.

A state arises by way of root condition (*hetupaccaya*). Dependent on a state that is neither-with-root-nor-root and neither-without-root-nor-root, a state that is neither-without-root-nor-root and with-root arises by way of root condition.

Dependent on a state that is neither-with-root-nor-root and neither-without-root-nor-root, states that are neither-with-root-nor-root and with-root, and neither-without-root-nor-root and with-root, arise by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.)

In the case of root condition, nine; in the case of object condition, four; in the case of predominance condition, five ... [etc. ... in the case of mutuality condition, six ... [etc. ... in the case of prenascence and repetition conditions, two ... [etc. ... in the case of non-disappearance condition, nine. (The full detail applies everywhere.
Dependent on a state that is neither-root nor not-root, there arises a state that is neither-root nor not-root by way of root condition.
(Abbreviated. In the case of root condition, one ... [etc. ... in the case of non-disappearance condition, one. (In all cases, one.)

Dependent on a state that is neither-root-associated and not-root, [arises a state] … (Abbreviated. Under root-condition there are nine; under object-condition four; under predominance-condition five … pe … under mutuality-condition six … pe … under prenascence and repetition-conditions two … pe … under non-disappearance-condition nine.

Dependent on a state that is neither-root-dissociated and not-not-root … Dependent on a state that is both not-root and not-rootless and is not-root … pe … Dependent on a state that is both not-rootless and not-not-root and is not-root … pe … [End.]

Dependent on a state that is neither-root nor dissociated from root and is itself not-root … dependent on a state that is both not-root and dissociated from root and is itself not-root … dependent on a state that is dissociated from root and is itself not-root … dependent on a state that is not-root, not-root-caused,
and is itself not-root … dependent on a state that is not-root, not-root-caused, and is itself not-root … (Abbreviated.)

In the case of the root condition, there are nine; in the object condition, four; in the predominance condition, five …pe… in the mutuality condition, six …pe… in the prenascence and repetition conditions, two …pe… in the non-disappearance condition, nine.
